in_sanskrit.name: हिरुणिका
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Hirunika is derived from the Sanskrit word हिरू (Hiru), which means 'head' and निका (Nikā), which means 'Goddess'. The name Hirunika signifies the Goddess who resides on the head. In Hindu mythology, the Goddess Shringini, also known as Shringamata or Shringaraparvathi, is the Goddess of the head and is often depicted as the consort of Lord Shiva. The name Hirunika may be used as a tribute to this revered deity.

historical_references.reference: Hirunika was a legendary queen of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling in the late 2nd or early 1st century BCE. She is best known for her contributions to the construction of the Prakasasila Dam and the Agastya Theertham tank in Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh.
